def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customer_ids = instance["customer_ids"]
    customers = set(customer_ids)
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    cust_list = list(customer_ids)

    def route_load(r):
        s = 0
        for v in r:
            s += demands[v]
        return s

    def route_cost(r):
        if not r:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][r[0]] + matrix[r[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(r) - 1):
            c += matrix[r[i]][r[i + 1]]
        return c

    def total_cost(routes):
        return sum(route_cost(r) for r in routes)

    def oriented_merge(routes, pos_in_route, i, j):

        ri = pos_in_route[i][0]
        rj = pos_in_route[j][0]
        if ri == rj:
            return False
        load_i = route_load(routes[ri])
        load_j = route_load(routes[rj])
        if load_i + load_j > capacity:
            return False

        # pos_in_route stores (route_index, side), where side 0 means left end, 1 right end
        side_i = pos_in_route[i][1]
        side_j = pos_in_route[j][1]

        # Determine concatenation order/orientation for a valid CW merge:
        # We only merge right end of one with left end of the other: routes[ri] + routes[rj]
        # after possible reversals.
        if side_i == 0:
            # i at left end -> reverse route ri to make i at right end
            routes[ri] = list(reversed(routes[ri]))
            # update side info for ri endpoints will be fixed by rebuild
        if side_j == 1:
            # j at right end -> reverse route rj to make j at left end
            routes[rj] = list(reversed(routes[rj]))

        # Now i should be at right end of ri and j at left end of rj
        ri = pos_in_route[i][0]
        rj = pos_in_route[j][0]
        if ri == rj:
            return False
        if route_load(routes[ri]) + route_load(routes[rj]) > capacity:
            return False

        new_route = routes[ri] + routes[rj]
        # Remove higher index first to keep indices valid
        a, b = ri, rj
        if a > b:
            a, b = b, a
        routes.pop(b)
        routes.pop(a)
        routes.append(new_route)
        return True

        # pos_in_route[v] = (route_index, side), only valid for endpoint customers
        pos = {}
        for idx, r in enumerate(routes):
            if r:
                pos[r[0]] = (idx, 0)
                pos[r[-1]] = (idx, 1)
        return pos

    def build_clarke_wright():
        # Start with each customer in its own route, then savings merges.
        routes = [[i] for i in cust_list]
        if not routes:
            return []

        pos_in_route = rebuild_pos(routes)

        # Prepare savings list
        # s(i,j) = d0i + d0j - dij
        savings = []
        for a_i in range(len(cust_list)):
            i = cust_list[a_i]
            for b_i in range(a_i + 1, len(cust_list)):
                j = cust_list[b_i]
                s = matrix[depot][i] + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
                # deterministic tie-break: larger s first, then smaller lexicographic pair
                savings.append((s, i, j))
        savings.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1], x[2]))

        # Greedy merges following CW feasibility
        # We rebuild pos occasionally, but keep deterministic.
